tools.name: list_cities
tools.description: Use this when someone asks which cities WonderKit covers or needs a valid city key. Lists cities that have a published city guide of real things to do, with their keys. Reads public guides only; it cannot plan, save, or look up a private trip.

tools.name: find_activities
tools.description: Use this when someone asks what to do in one city: weekend ideas, events, food, or kid-friendly, date-night, or group activities. Returns published picks from the WonderKit city guide and the page URL. Returns single activities, not multi-day plans, and cannot see anyone's own trips.

city.description: City name or WonderKit city key, such as "Paris" or "paris-france".

audience.description: Who the plan is for: families, friends, or couples.

query.description: Optional words to match against activity titles and descriptions, such as "museums" or "dinner". Plurals match singulars.

tools.name: list_itineraries
tools.description: Use this when someone wants to browse WonderKit's public multi-day itineraries and place guides, for all cities or one city and audience. Plans that are in season this month come first. Each summary has dayCount (days or themed sections) and stopCount (anchors plus backups; before 2026-09-28 stopCount held the day count). Browses by city and audience only; it does not rank by a free-text description. Does not book or edit a trip.

city.description: City name or WonderKit city key, such as "Paris" or "paris-france".

audience.description: Who the plan is for: families, friends, or couples.

tools.name: search_itineraries
tools.description: Use this when someone describes the trip they want, such as "romantic weekend in October", "museums with kids", or "Christmas markets", and needs matching public itineraries across cities. Ranks by the words they used, who it is for, and season fit. Pass a city to stay in one city. Do not use it to create or save a trip; it only reads published guides.

query.description: What they want, in their words, such as "romantic weekend", "museums with kids", or "fall foliage". Plurals match singulars.

city.description: City name or WonderKit city key, such as "Paris" or "paris-france".

audience.description: Who the plan is for: families, friends, or couples.

season.description: Season they are travelling in. "now" means the current month. Northern-hemisphere seasons.

month.description: Travel month, 1-12. Boosts plans whose peak months include it. Wins over season.

shape.description: day-plan for a day-by-day plan, places-guide for a themed list of places.

limit.description: How many results to return, up to 8.

tools.name: get_itinerary
tools.description: Use this when someone wants the full plan for one public itinerary, by its slug: day-by-day or themed stops with real venues and map links, rainy-day and where-to-eat sections, and the best season. Returns dayCount and stopCount (anchors plus backups; before 2026-09-28 stopCount held the day count), the page URL, and planUrl, which opens the WonderKit planner prefilled from this plan. Read-only; it cannot change a plan.

city.description: City name or WonderKit city key, such as "Paris" or "paris-france".

slug.description: Itinerary slug from list_itineraries or search_itineraries, such as "3-day-weekend-for-couples".

tools.name: plan_trip_link
tools.description: Use this when someone wants to start planning their own trip to a destination in WonderKit. Returns one guest-planner link with the city (and vibe) filled in, plus a one-line description. It creates nothing and cannot book; the person adds dates and travelers in the planner. The link is a planner, not a citable guide page.

city.description: Destination as the person said it, such as "Lisbon" or "Asheville, NC". Any city works.

startDate.description: First day, YYYY-MM-DD, if they gave one.

endDate.description: Last day, YYYY-MM-DD, if they gave one.

vibe.description: The feel they want, if they said.

kidsAges.description: Ages of children travelling, if any.

tools.name: continue_in_wonderkit
tools.description: Use this when someone wants to save, share, or keep working on a plan from a public guide or itinerary. Returns the WonderKit web links for that city guide, itinerary, and the guest planner. This server cannot save or share anything itself.

city.description: City name or WonderKit city key, such as "Paris" or "paris-france".

slug.description: Optional itinerary slug to link a specific public plan.
